issues.legal_issue: Female relatives of a husband or male partner may be made respondents in a complaint under domestic-violence law filed by an aggrieved wife or woman in a relationship in the nature of marriage.
material_facts: An aggrieved wife filed a domestic-violence complaint against her husband and his mother and sister, both of whom were women.
The lower courts treated the definition of respondent as excluding female relatives and ordered their names deleted from the proceedings.
The Supreme Court considered whether the statutory proviso permitted a complaint against those female relatives.
issues.conclusion: The Court held that female relatives are not excluded from the complaint and set aside the decisions deleting them from the proceedings; the trial court was to proceed against them.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 2(q) of the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005, the proviso extends the main definition of respondent by allowing an aggrieved wife or woman in a relationship in the nature of marriage to complain against a relative of the husband or male partner. The term “relative” is not restricted to male relatives, and the Court identified no earlier cases on which it relied.

rule.if: complaint_is_under_domestic_violence_law and complainant_is_aggrieved_wife_or_partner and named_person_is_relative_of_husband_or_partner and named_person_is_female

predicates.complaint_is_under_domestic_violence_law: The complainant filed a complaint seeking relief under domestic-violence law.
predicates.complainant_is_aggrieved_wife_or_partner: The complainant is an aggrieved wife or a woman living in a relationship in the nature of marriage.
predicates.named_person_is_relative_of_husband_or_p: The person named in the complaint is a relative of the complainant’s husband or male partner.
predicates.named_person_is_female: The person named in the complaint is female.
predicates.female_relative_can_be_named_as_responde: A female relative of the husband or male partner may be named as a respondent in the complaint.

issues.definition: When an aggrieved wife or woman in a marriage-like relationship files a domestic-violence complaint against a female relative of her husband or male partner, that relative may be named as a respondent.
